home.cultureText: Lunar New Year is the most important traditional festival across many Asian cultures. 2027 welcomes the Year of the Goat, a sign of peace, kindness, and creativity. The festival brings these traditions to everyone in the Mid-South.

about.title: About the Festival
about.mission: The Mid-South Lunar New Year Festival showcases the historical origins and cultural significance of the Lunar New Year to residents of all backgrounds in the Memphis area through performances, food, markets, and interactive activities. It aims to promote understanding and friendship among citizens from different cultures and to celebrate the vibrant spirit of the Memphis Chinese community.
about.org: The Mid-South Chinese Chamber of Commerce (MCCC) is a non-profit organization serving the Chinese business community in the Greater Memphis area. MCCC supports the development of Chinese businesses and promotes exchange between the Chinese community and the wider society.

culture.title: Reunion dinner
culture.text: Families gather on New Year's Eve for a feast. Dumplings and fish are served for wealth and abundance.

culture.title: Red and gold
culture.text: Red scares away bad luck and gold stands for prosperity. Homes are decorated with couplets and lanterns.

culture.title: Red envelopes
culture.text: Elders give money in red envelopes to children as a blessing for the year ahead.

culture.title: Year of the Goat
culture.text: 2027 is the Year of the Goat, associated with gentleness, creativity, and peace.

culture.title: Lantern Festival
culture.text: The celebration ends on the fifteenth day with lanterns, riddles, and sweet rice balls.

culture.title: Lion and dragon dances
culture.text: Drums and dancing creatures bring good fortune and drive away evil spirits.
